newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire envoy says he has resigned for French trial.
newsitem.headline: Zaire envoy says he has resigned for French trial.

text.p: Zaire's former envoy to France says he has resigned to stand trial in this country for killing two boys in a traffic accident in the Riviera resort of Menton.

"I have decided of my own free will to resign, which the head of state has accepted, and which opens the way to a trial," envoy Ramazani Baya told French TF1 television in an interview broadcast on Saturday.
Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko said last week he had relieved Baya of his functions and diplomatic immunity so that he could stand trial for the accident last November.

French police have said Baya, who was on his way to visit Mobutu at the Zairean leader's Riviera villa, was driving at more than twice the legal speed limit when he hit Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing.
TF1 said the former envoy left Kinshasa on Saturday and was expected in Paris later in the day.
He could face up to three years in jail if convicted of manslaughter.
Relatives of the boys had been demonstrating to demand that he be brought to trial, and the French government had asked Kinshasa to waive his immunity.
"As a father myself, I realise the tragedy and the (parents') suffering. I know that only the trial they are demanding could bring them some comfort," Baya said.
"I will not be in peace until this this judgment has been passed," he said.
Patrick Lenoir, the father of one of the dead boys, welcomed Baya's statement. "I think he realised our tragedy and he sounded sincere," he said.
Mobutu, who is a close ally of France in Africa, is resting at his Riviera villa after cancer treatment.
